author.zh: 罗伯特·路易斯·史蒂文森

year_display.zh: 1878 年；1881 年收入《致少男少女》

edition.en: The last essay of Virginibus Puerisque, and Other Papers, in the 1897 Chatto & Windus edition as transcribed by Project Gutenberg (eBook 386), collated with the first edition (London: C. Kegan Paul, 1881), which reads “advanced with another stride” where the later edition has “by another stride” and prints “back-shop” and “wild fire” as two words. The capitals of the opening word, a printer’s convention, are set in ordinary case; Stevenson’s footnotes belong to other essays in the book.
edition.zh: 《致少男少女及其他》的最后一篇，据古登堡计划电子书第 386 号所录 1897 年查托与温达斯版，并与初版（伦敦：C. 基根·保罗出版社，1881）对校：初版作“advanced with another stride”，后来的版本作“by another stride”；初版“back-shop”“wild fire”分写。开篇首词的全大写是排印惯例，改为常规大小写；书中史蒂文森的脚注属于其他篇目。

basis.en: First published in 1878 and collected in 1881; Robert Louis Stevenson died in 1894.
basis.zh: 1878 年首次发表，1881 年结集；史蒂文森卒于 1894 年。

note.en: Stevenson wrote this in 1878, when the first electric arc lamps were going up in Paris and London and the lamplighter’s evening round seemed to be coming to an end. It is a mock-heroic history of street light, from the stable lantern to the gas lamp, and a plea against the glare that was about to replace it. Read it beside his poem The Lamplighter on the poetry shelf; the man with the ladder appears in both.
note.zh: 史蒂文森写这篇文章是在 1878 年，那时巴黎和伦敦的街头刚刚立起第一批电弧灯，点灯人傍晚的巡行眼看就要走到尽头。这是一部仿英雄体的街灯简史，从马厩灯笼写到煤气灯，也是对即将取代它的那种强光的抗辩。可以和诗歌架上他的《点灯人》对照着读：那个扛梯子的人在两篇里都出现了。

excerpt.orig: The city-folk had stars of their own; biddable, domesticated stars.
excerpt.en: The city-folk had stars of their own; biddable, domesticated stars.
excerpt.zh: 城里人有了自己的星星，驯服的、家养的星星。

gloss.en: The town as a rabbit warren of burgesses, its citizens.
gloss.zh: 把城镇比作市民们的兔子窝。burgess，市民。

gloss.en: An iron basket of burning pitch or wood, set on a pole or a wall as a beacon.
gloss.zh: 火篮：装着燃烧的松脂或木柴的铁篮，架在杆上或墙上当作照明。

gloss.at: stable lanthorns two stories in height
gloss.en: Lanthorn is the old spelling of lantern, from the thin plates of horn that once served as its panes.
gloss.zh: lanthorn 是 lantern（灯笼）的旧拼法，因为早先灯笼用薄角片代替玻璃。

gloss.en: The Pharos was the great lighthouse of ancient Alexandria; here, the lantern carried through the streets.
gloss.zh: 法罗斯是古代亚历山大港的大灯塔；这里指拎着在街上走的灯笼。

gloss.en: A kennel is a street gutter.
gloss.zh: kennel 在这里指街边的阴沟。

gloss.en: In Greek myth Prometheus stole fire from the gods and gave it to mankind.
gloss.zh: 希腊神话中，普罗米修斯从众神那里盗火给人类。

gloss.en: A small lantern with a thick, convex glass lens, the lamplighter’s torch.
gloss.zh: 牛眼灯：装有厚凸透镜的小灯笼，点灯人用来点火的工具。

gloss.at: from the Alexandra to the Crystal Palace
gloss.en: The two great exhibition halls on the heights at the northern and southern edges of Victorian London.
gloss.zh: 亚历山德拉宫和水晶宫，维多利亚时代伦敦南北两端高地上的两座大型展览馆。

gloss.en: “Let there be light”: Genesis 1:3 in the Latin Bible.
gloss.zh: “要有光”，拉丁文《圣经·创世记》第一章第三节。

gloss.en: In the late 1870s Manchester’s plan to turn Thirlmere in the Lake District into a reservoir was opposed by artists and writers, Ruskin among them.
gloss.zh: 19 世纪 70 年代末，曼彻斯特计划把湖区的瑟尔米尔湖改成水库，遭到许多艺术家和作家反对，罗斯金也在其中。

gloss.at: in the place before the Opera portico
gloss.en: In 1878 the avenue and square before the Paris Opéra were lit by Yablochkov electric candles, among the first electric street lamps.
gloss.zh: 1878 年，巴黎歌剧院前的大道和广场装上了亚布洛奇科夫电烛，这是最早的电力街灯之一。

gloss.en: The lightning bolt; levin is an old word for lightning.
gloss.zh: 闪电的火把。levin 是古词，意为闪电。

gloss.at: the light of the Terror that Flieth
gloss.en: From Psalm 91: “the terror by night” and “the arrow that flieth by day”.
gloss.zh: 语出《圣经·诗篇》第九十一篇：“黑夜的惊骇”“白日飞的箭”。

note.en: A witty mock-history of street lighting by a young Stevenson, charming in its conceits; a slight occasional piece whose argument against electric light was lost before it was made.
note.zh: 青年史蒂文森戏仿史诗写街灯的历史，奇思可喜；只是轻巧的应时小文，反对电灯的理由注定无人采纳。
